statement: I notice opportunities to start conversations with people who might benefit from my coaching.
I pay so much attention to whether it is a good moment to make contact that I often hold back from starting a conversation.
I notice when there is a natural opportunity to start a conversation and choose an appropriate moment to do so.
I hesitate to start conversations, even when there seems to be a good opportunity to make contact.
I am comfortable letting conversations arise naturally rather than actively looking for new ones.
I stay focused on what I am already doing rather than looking for opportunities to start new conversations.
I can introduce what I offer clearly when it is relevant to the conversation.
I bring up my coaching services before I have understood whether they are relevant to the person.
I find natural opportunities to mention my coaching services as a conversation develops.
I overthink how to mention my coaching services and sometimes avoid mentioning them at all.
I am comfortable letting a conversation develop without actively steering it towards my coaching services.
I find it difficult to introduce my coaching services, even when there is a relevant opportunity to do so.
I put people at ease when I first start talking with them.
I focus so much on being friendly that I avoid talking about the coaching support I offer.
I build a connection naturally as conversations get going.
I can become preoccupied with overcoming awkwardness, which makes it harder for me to connect naturally.
I can keep an initial conversation straightforward and professional without needing to build a personal connection.
I can be so focused on the practical purpose of a conversation that I overlook opportunities to connect.
I listen closely to what someone says and notice what matters most to them.
I focus so much on listening for every detail that I can lose sight of where the conversation needs to go.
I listen for the main things someone wants to achieve and respond to what I hear.
I sometimes miss details that would help me understand what someone wants.
I keep the conversation moving, drawing on the key things I hear as I go.
I become so focused on what I want to say that I miss important things the other person tells me.
I use clear, purposeful questions to explore what someone wants to achieve.
I ask so many directed questions that I leave little room for the other person to explain things in their own way.
I ask enough questions to understand what someone wants while keeping the conversation moving.
I rush to fill pauses rather than giving the other person time to think and respond.
I am comfortable letting the other person shape the conversation rather than taking the lead myself.
I move into advice or solutions before I have properly explored what the other person wants or needs.
I make it easy for someone to talk openly about what matters to them.
I focus so much on keeping the conversation comfortable that I avoid exploring things that may be harder to talk about.
I build enough connection for the conversation to move beyond basic facts and goals.
I can struggle to build enough connection to explore what really matters to someone.
I keep the conversation practical and professional without needing to explore things at a more personal level.
I tend to keep conversations at a surface level even when understanding more would be useful.
I tailor my recommendation to what the person has told me.
I focus so much on finding the right recommendation that I hesitate to make a clear one.
I explain how my recommendation connects to what the person wants to achieve.
I sometimes make a recommendation without clearly connecting it to what the person has told me.
I am comfortable recommending an approach I know works without tailoring every detail to the individual.
I tend to recommend my preferred approach without checking how well it fits what the person has told me.
I make a clear recommendation and invite the person to take a specific next step.
I push for a commitment before I have given the person enough space to decide.
I make a recommendation and help the conversation move towards a next step without forcing the pace.
I can make the next step less clear by offering too many options.
I am comfortable presenting the options and leaving the person to decide what they want to do next.
I avoid asking whether someone wants to take a clear next step with me.
I present my recommendation in a way that connects with what matters to the person.
I focus so much on preserving the relationship that I avoid being direct about the next step.
I check how my recommendation lands with the person before discussing what happens next.
I can become so focused on keeping things positive that I avoid checking for doubts or concerns about my recommendation.
I focus on explaining clearly what working with me would involve, without needing to build further personal connection.
I can be so focused on explaining what I offer that I overlook whether the person feels connected to it.
